alquilar-autocaravana-valencia.metaTitle: Motorhome Hire Valencia: Requirements, Price & Deposit | Camper Retreat VLC
alquilar-autocaravana-valencia.metaDescription: Campervan rental in Valencia: age, licence, price per night, what's included, the €900 deposit, mileage and cancellation.
alquilar-autocaravana-valencia.h1: Motorhome hire in Valencia: requirements, price and deposit
alquilar-autocaravana-valencia.intro: If you're looking for campervan or motorhome rental in Valencia, this guide sums up what you need to know before you book: who can drive, how much each night costs, what the price includes, how the security deposit works and what happens if your plans change. All details refer to our McLouis Yearling 89 motorhome for up to 5 people.

paragraphs: A standard car driving licence (category B) is all you need to drive the motorhome; no special licence is required.
list: Minimum age of 25 for the main renter and for every additional driver.
Category B driving licence held for more than 2 years. If you live outside the EU, you also need an International Driving Permit.
A bank card to pay for the booking online and for the €900 security deposit.
Pick-up and drop-off at Carrer de Nino Bravo, 3, Valencia.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to rent a motorhome in Valencia?
paragraphs: The price depends on the season. These are the nightly rates excluding VAT (21% is added), with the minimum stay for each season:
list: Low season: €90 per night, minimum 3 nights.
Mid season: €125 per night, minimum 3 nights.
High season: €155 per night, minimum 4 nights.
Peak season (Christmas and August): €185 per night, minimum 5 nights.

paragraphs: Discounts can be combined. The longer you stay, the lower your nightly rate:
list: 5% off for stays of 7 nights or more, and 10% off from 14 nights.
Occasional promo codes, applied in the price calculator before you pay.

paragraphs: 7 nights in February 2027 (low season), paying 100% when booking: €784 including VAT, around €112 per night. This includes the €50 final cleaning fee and the 5% long-stay discount.

7 nights in July 2027 (high season), paying 50% when booking: €1,308 including VAT, of which €654 is paid when you book and the rest when you pick up the motorhome. The exact totals for your dates are shown in the booking calculator.
The final price already includes VAT and the following:
list: Two gas bottles and chemical toilet capsules.
Free parking for your car at our premises during the rental.
Camping table and chairs, three beach chairs, a parasol and awning, Smart TV, kitchenware, pillows and blankets.

paragraphs: Each night includes 100 km. If you plan to drive more, you can add 200 km per night (€20 per night) or unlimited mileage (€40 per night). Any kilometres beyond your allowance cost €0.30 each.

The motorhome is handed over with a full tank and must be returned the same way. It should also be returned clean inside, with the grey water and toilet cassette emptied and the fresh water tank full.
In the calculator you can add per-booking extras: bike (€90), SUP board (€90), additional driver (€50), bed linen (€20), towels (€15) and barbecue (€15).

The refundable security deposit is €900 and is paid before handover, preferably as a pre-authorisation on the main driver's card. After the motorhome has been inspected, it is refunded within 14 working days of the return at the latest, provided the vehicle is in the same condition as at handover. The insurance is comprehensive: in the event of damage, the most you pay is the applicable excess, €900.

Choose your dates and pick-up and drop-off times in the calendar on campervlc.com, add any extras and pay by card. You can pay 50% when booking and the rest at pick-up, or 100% up front. You'll receive a confirmation email with your booking number.
With that number and your email address you can change your dates or add extras on the manage-booking page, up to 48 hours before handover.
You can cancel free of charge within 24 hours of booking if handover is more than 7 days away. After that, the amount we keep depends on how far in advance you cancel:

faq.q: What licence do I need to drive the motorhome?
faq.a: A standard category B car licence, held for more than 2 years, and a minimum age of 25. If you live outside the EU, you also need an International Driving Permit. The motorhome is 3.30 m high, so check the height limits of car parks and tunnels.

faq.q: How many people does it sleep?
faq.a: It has 5 travelling seats and 5 berths, with a maximum payload of 500 kg for passengers and luggage.

faq.q: Can I bring my dog?
faq.a: Yes. Pets travel for a 50 € supplement per booking. If on return there is a smell of tobacco or animals that requires special treatment, the actual cost is charged, up to a maximum of €300.

faq.q: What happens if I return the motorhome later?
faq.a: If you choose your return time when booking, returning up to 6 hours after the pick-up time costs 50% of a rental day, and more than 6 hours costs a full day. An unagreed late return is charged at €50 per hour, so always let us know.

faq.q: How do I pay?
faq.a: You pay for the booking online by bank card, securely via Stripe: 50% when booking and the rest at pick-up, or 100% up front. The €900 security deposit is paid before handover, preferably as a card pre-authorisation.

cta.text: Check the exact price for your dates and book in minutes.

mejor-epoca-autocaravana-valencia.metaTitle: Best Time for a Motorhome Trip in Valencia: 2027 Seasons | Camper Retreat VLC
mejor-epoca-autocaravana-valencia.metaDescription: When to hire a motorhome in Valencia: 2027 low, mid, high and peak seasons, nightly prices, minimum stays, Fallas, Easter and summer.
mejor-epoca-autocaravana-valencia.h1: Best time for a motorhome trip in Valencia: 2027 seasons and prices
mejor-epoca-autocaravana-valencia.intro: You can tour Valencia and the Mediterranean coast by motorhome all year round. What changes with the date is the atmosphere, the crowds and the price. This guide helps you choose when to travel and shows the 2027 season calendar for our motorhome.

paragraphs: Winter on the Valencian coast is mild, summer is hot and humid, and spring and autumn are the most comfortable months to sleep in the motorhome without relying on air conditioning. Our motorhome has air conditioning and heating, so you can travel comfortably in any season.

sections.h2: Low season (€90 per night, minimum 3 nights)
paragraphs: This is the quietest and most affordable time, ideal for travelling at a relaxed pace with few people on the beaches and at motorhome service areas. In 2027 low season covers these dates:

sections.h2: Mid season (€125 per night, minimum 3 nights)
paragraphs: Spring and early autumn bring good weather and mid-range prices. 2027 dates:

sections.h2: High season (€155 per night, minimum 4 nights)
paragraphs: It covers the most popular festivals and long weekends, plus summer. Book well ahead for these 2027 dates:
list: 22 to 24 January (San Vicente Mártir long weekend).
15 to 21 March (Fallas, Valencia's famous March festival).
25 March to 5 April (Semana Santa, Holy Week and Easter).

sections.h2: Peak season (€185 per night, minimum 5 nights)
paragraphs: These are the dates of highest demand:
list: 22 December to 6 January (Christmas and New Year).

paragraphs: Prices are per night and 21% VAT is added. If you can choose, travel outside long weekends and summer: you save on the rate and find more space at motorhome areas. Stays of 7 nights or more get a 5% discount, stays of 14 nights or more get 10%.

For Fallas, Semana Santa, the October long weekend and August, it's best to book several months in advance, as the calendar fills up early. You can check real-time availability in the booking calendar on campervlc.com. For itinerary ideas, see our motorhome routes from Valencia.

faq.q: When is it cheapest to rent a motorhome in Valencia?
faq.a: In low season (€90 per night in 2027): January, February and most of March, late October and November. On top of that, stays of 7 and 14 nights get 5% and 10% discounts.

faq.q: How far in advance should I book?
faq.a: For Fallas, Semana Santa, summer and long weekends, it's best to book months ahead. The rest of the year there is usually availability at shorter notice; you can book up to 24 hours before pick-up.

faq.q: Are the seasons the same every year?
faq.a: No. The dates in this calendar are for 2027 and follow Valencia's official holidays and long weekends, which change every year. The booking calculator always shows the exact price for your dates.

cta.text: Choose your dates and see the exact price before you pay.

autocaravana-5-plazas-valencia.h1: 5-berth motorhome with shower, air conditioning and pet friendly in Valencia
autocaravana-5-plazas-valencia.intro: Here is the full spec sheet for the motorhome we rent out in Valencia: a 2024 McLouis Yearling 89 on a Renault Master base, designed for up to 5 people travelling with all equipment included.

list: Model: McLouis Yearling 89 on a Renault Master (2024), diesel.
Height: 3.30 m. Maximum payload (passengers and luggage): 500 kg.
Air conditioning, heating, fridge-freezer, hot water, shower and toilet.

paragraphs: Kitchenware is included in the price: plates, glasses, coffee cups, spoons and teaspoons, forks, table knives, kitchen knives and serrated knives, a wooden chopping board, spatulas, 3 frying pans, a medium saucepan, a saucepan with a glass lid, a salad bowl, a corkscrew and a moka pot.
Pillows and blankets are included. If you'd like bed linen, you can add it to your booking for €20 (bath towels, €15).

Two tables and four camping chairs, three beach chairs, a parasol and an awning, so you can enjoy your stop outside the motorhome. As per-booking extras you can add a bike (€90), a SUP board (€90) and a barbecue (€15).

Two gas bottles for the fridge, heating, hot water and gas hob, plus chemical toilet capsules. A welcome kit with toilet paper, coffee and soap. 100 km per night included and free parking for your car at our premises during the rental.
Pets travel for a 50 € supplement per booking. A free child seat is available on request for travelling with children.

Pick-up and drop-off are at Carrer de Nino Bravo, 3, Valencia. At handover we sign a condition report for the motorhome and show you how all the equipment works. If you have any questions, you can message us on WhatsApp.

faq.q: Can 5 people sleep in the motorhome?
faq.a: Yes, it has 5 berths and 5 travelling seats. The maximum payload for passengers and luggage is 500 kg.

faq.q: Does it have a shower and toilet?
faq.a: Yes: a shower with hot water and a cassette toilet. It is returned with the cassette emptied and clean.

faq.q: Does it have air conditioning and heating?
faq.a: Yes, the motorhome has air conditioning and heating, plus a fridge-freezer.

faq.q: Is it pet friendly?
faq.a: Yes. Pets are welcome, for a 50 € supplement per booking.

cta.text: Book the motorhome and check the exact price for your dates.

paises-autocaravana-alquiler.metaTitle: Rental motorhome abroad: allowed and forbidden countries
paises-autocaravana-alquiler.metaDescription: Our Valencia motorhome can go to Portugal, France and 27 more countries with written permission. Insurance, ferries, vignettes and why not Morocco.
paises-autocaravana-alquiler.h1: Which countries can you drive a rental motorhome to from Valencia
paises-autocaravana-alquiler.intro: Almost every customer asks us the same thing before booking: can I cross into Portugal, drive up to France or go down to Morocco with the motorhome? Here is the full answer, taken from the rental contract (clauses 7.1 to 7.4), plus what you need to know in each country about tolls, vignettes and low emission zones. Our motorhome is a McLouis Yearling 89 on a Renault Master from 2024, diesel, 3.30 m high, with 5 seats. You drive it on a category B licence, so for tolls and vignettes it counts as a vehicle up to 3.5 t.

sections.h2: How it works: Spain by default, 29 countries with written permission
paragraphs: Without any extra step, the motorhome may only be driven in Spain (clause 7.1). To leave the country you need the owner's prior written permission.

Ask for it when you book or, at the latest, before you set off, by WhatsApp (+34 624 038 085) or by email (camper.retreat.alicante@gmail.com). Tell us the countries, the rough dates and whether you plan to take a ferry. We send you the permission in writing and you keep it in the motorhome together with the contract.

For long trips, check your mileage: every night includes 100 km, and in the booking calculator you can add 200 km per night or unlimited mileage. With the permission you can travel to these 29 countries (clause 7.2):
list: Southern Europe: Portugal, France, Andorra, Italy, Malta, Greece and Cyprus.
Central Europe: Germany, Switzerland, Austria, Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg.
Northern Europe: Denmark, Sweden, Norway, Finland and Iceland.
Baltic states and Eastern Europe: Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia, Poland, Czechia, Slovakia and Hungary.
British Isles: Great Britain and Ireland.

paragraphs: The motorhome has fully comprehensive insurance with an excess of 900 € per damage item (clause 11.1). Own damage cover only applies in Spain, Andorra and the countries of the Multilateral Guarantee Agreement, the green card system shared by European insurers. All 29 countries on the list are inside it.
In those countries the Spanish number plate counts as proof of insurance and no green card is needed. Even so, always carry the insurance certificate, which travels with the vehicle documents.
Outside the authorised area there is no own damage cover. If something happens there, you pay the full damage, with no excess cap (clause 11.4.d).

Putting the motorhome on a ferry, a train or any other transport needs prior written permission (clauses 6.1.h and 7.4). On top of that, the insurance does not cover own damage or fire during sea or air transport. From the start of loading to the end of unloading, manoeuvres inside the port included, you pay any damage at its real cost, with no excess cap.
Inside ports and airports you may only drive on public access roads and car parks and on the authorised boarding route. Quays, loading areas, runways and operational areas are off limits.

This also applies to the Balearic Islands. They are Spain, but you reach them by ferry: you need the same permission and the same insurance exclusion applies during the crossing. The Eurotunnel train under the Channel also needs written permission.

sections.h2: Tolls, vignettes and charges that arrive later
paragraphs: Each country charges for its roads in its own way: toll booths, electronic tolls by number plate or a time-based vignette. Where there is a vignette, the motorhome falls into the category for vehicles up to 3.5 t. Buy vignettes on each country's official website; plenty of reseller sites add a commission.

Some tolls and city charges arrive weeks later, addressed to the vehicle owner. Under the contract, those amounts are charged to your card up to 12 months after the rental, always with the supporting document (clause 5.6). Paying on time during the trip saves you surcharges.
Keep the vehicle's own limits in mind too: 110 km/h maximum even where the road allows more, and no passages lower than 3.30 m (clause 6.4).
It is the trip we are asked about most and the easiest one: from Valencia you get there on dual carriageways in one long day of driving.

Many Portuguese motorways have electronic tolls with no booths: a gantry reads the number plate. With a Spanish plate you need to link a bank card to the plate (EasyToll) or rent a Via Verde Visitors device before the first tolled stretch. The motorhome pays as class 2.

The contract asks for one specific thing for Portugal: when you come back you must be able to show that you paid the tolls. If you cannot, the outstanding tolls are charged plus a 50 € handling fee (clause 7.2). Worth seeing: the Atlantic coast, from the Algarve to Lisbon and Porto.

sections.h2: France: class 3 péage and the Crit'Air sticker
paragraphs: French motorways have toll booths. Motorhomes 3 m high or more pay class 3, and ours is 3.30 m. Without a toll tag, use the card payment lanes that have a height gauge.
To enter the low emission zones (ZFE) of cities such as Paris or Lyon you need the Crit'Air sticker, which you order on the official site certificat-air.gouv.fr. A diesel from 2024 gets Crit'Air 2.
Worth seeing: the lavender fields of Valensole in Provence, which bloom in early summer.
You get there via La Seu d'Urgell. Andorra has no motorways and no vignette; the Envalira tunnel towards France does charge a toll.

Andorra is not in the European Union, so there are customs checks on the way in and on the way back to Spain, with purchase limits for tobacco and alcohol. Mountain roads have long descents: go down in a low gear so the brakes do not overheat.
Worth seeing: the cable cars and mountains of Grandvalira, in winter and in summer.

sections.h2: Italy: class B autostrada and ZTL zones
paragraphs: Italian motorways have toll booths. Two-axle vehicles more than 1.30 m high at the front axle pay class B, and that includes the motorhome.
Almost every city centre has a ZTL, a limited traffic zone watched by cameras. If you drive in without a permit, the fine arrives months later. Park outside and go in on foot or by public transport.
Worth seeing: Rome and the Colosseum. Leave the motorhome at a campsite on the outskirts and go in by metro or bus. Italian ports are also where the ferries to Greece and Malta leave from.

To use Swiss motorways you need the vignette, which only comes as an annual one: 40 CHF for vehicles up to 3.5 t. Since 2023 there is an e-vignette linked to the number plate, sold on the official site via.admin.ch.
Switzerland is not in the European Union: there are customs checks and you may be asked for the contract and the permission. Mountain passes are steep; use engine braking on the way down.
Worth seeing: the Alpine lakes and passes, best in summer, when all the passes are open.

Austrian motorways and expressways require a vignette for vehicles up to 3.5 t. The digital vignette is linked to the number plate and sold in the official ASFINAG shop, for 1 day, 10 days, 2 months or a year.

Watch the timing: a 2-month or annual digital vignette bought online as a private person only becomes valid 18 days after purchase. The 1-day and 10-day ones are valid straight away. Some tunnels and mountain sections have a separate toll.
Worth seeing: Vienna and its State Opera.

sections.h2: Germany: toll-free autobahn and the green sticker
paragraphs: Vehicles up to 3.5 t pay no toll and need no vignette on German motorways; only heavier vehicles pay the toll.

Around 35 cities have an environmental zone (Umweltzone) and require the green sticker (Umweltplakette), foreign vehicles included. Without it the fine is 100 €. Ask us whether the motorhome already has one; if not, you can order it online before the trip.

Germany is the way through to Denmark, Poland and Czechia, and it has plenty of well equipped motorhome stopovers (Stellplätze). Worth seeing: Neuschwanstein Castle in Bavaria, from the Marienbrücke bridge.

sections.h2: Belgium: LEZ zones with prior registration
paragraphs: Belgian motorways have no toll for vehicles up to 3.5 t.

Brussels, Antwerp and Ghent have a low emission zone (LEZ). A Euro 6 diesel may enter, but foreign vehicles have to register first, free of charge. Brussels and Flanders (Antwerp and Ghent) keep separate registers.
Worth seeing: the canals of Bruges, best explored on foot from a car park on the edge of town.
The Netherlands has no motorway tolls. You only pay in a few tunnels, such as the Westerschelde tunnel in Zeeland.

Several cities have an environmental zone (milieuzone) for older diesels; as a diesel from 2024, the motorhome meets the Euro 6 standard. Parking in city centres is expensive: use the P+R car parks on the outskirts.
Worth seeing: the windmills of Kinderdijk, near Rotterdam.

sections.h2: Luxembourg: no tolls and cheap diesel
paragraphs: Luxembourg has no tolls and no vignette, and diesel usually costs less than in the neighbouring countries. It is a good place to fill the tank.
Worth seeing: the Grund district, in the lower part of the capital.
You get there by land from Germany. Danish motorways have no toll, but the Great Belt (Storebælt) bridge and the Øresund bridge to Sweden do. On both, the motorhome pays according to its length.
Worth seeing: the Nyhavn harbour in Copenhagen.

sections.h2: Sweden: congestion tax in Stockholm and Gothenburg
paragraphs: From Denmark you cross the Øresund bridge, with no ferry. Sweden has hardly any road tolls, but Stockholm and Gothenburg charge a congestion tax by camera. For foreign plates the invoice is issued by Epass24 and goes to the vehicle owner, who passes it on to you.
Worth seeing: Gamla Stan, the old town of Stockholm.

Almost all Norwegian tolls are automatic (AutoPASS): a camera reads the number plate. Register the motorhome with Epass24 before the trip so you can pay by card and the invoices do not reach the owner later.
Many fjord routes include short ferries. They count as ferries under clause 7.4: include them in your permission request and remember that the insurance does not cover own damage during the crossing.
Norway is not in the European Union, so there are customs checks. Worth seeing: the Atlantic Road, between Molde and Kristiansund.

sections.h2: Finland: by land or by ferry
paragraphs: Finland has no road tolls. You get there by land around the Gulf of Bothnia through northern Sweden, or by ferry from Stockholm or Tallinn. If you choose the ferry, you need the permission described in clause 7.4.

It is a very long trip from Valencia: work out the kilometres carefully and consider unlimited mileage. Worth seeing: the reindeer of Finnish Lapland, for example around Kilpisjärvi in the far north-west.

sections.h2: Lithuania: the gateway to the Baltic states
paragraphs: From Poland you enter Lithuania on the Via Baltica, which continues through Latvia to Estonia. All three countries are in the European Union and the Schengen area.
Worth seeing: Trakai Castle, on an island in Lake Galvė, half an hour from Vilnius.
Latvia is the middle stretch of the Via Baltica. Riga's old town is small, with narrow streets: leave the motorhome at a campsite or a guarded car park and walk in.
Worth seeing: Riga's Town Hall Square and the House of the Blackheads.

sections.h2: Estonia: Tallinn and the ferry to Finland
paragraphs: Estonia is the end of the Via Baltica. Ferries to Helsinki leave from Tallinn; to take the motorhome on board you need written permission.
Worth seeing: the views over Tallinn's old town from Toompea hill.

Poland has no vignette. Since 2023 state motorways have been free for vehicles up to 3.5 t. You only pay on three concession sections: the A1 Gdańsk-Toruń, the A2 Świecko-Konin and the A4 Katowice-Kraków.
Worth seeing: Wawel Castle in Kraków, at the end of the tolled stretch of the A4.
Czech motorways require an e-vignette for vehicles up to 3.5 t. It is linked to the number plate, there is no sticker, and you buy it on the official site edalnice.cz.
Worth seeing: Charles Bridge in Prague.
As in Czechia, Slovak motorways and expressways require an e-vignette linked to the number plate. You buy it on the official site eznamka.sk.
Worth seeing: Bratislava Castle above the Danube.

Hungarian motorways require an e-matrica, the electronic vignette. Motorhomes registered as M1, up to 3.5 t and with no more than 7 seats go in category D1. Check the details in the registration certificate before you buy it.
Worth seeing: the Chain Bridge in Budapest, lit up at night.

Slovenia requires an e-vignette (e-vinjeta) on motorways and expressways. For vehicles up to 3.5 t, the class depends on the height at the front axle, with the limit at 1.30 m. Buy it only on the official DARS site and check the motorhome's class there.
Worth seeing: Lake Bled.

sections.h2: Croatia: tolls by section and the Pelješac bridge
paragraphs: Croatian motorways are tolled. In 2026 you still pay at booths; the country has announced a barrier-free system from March 2027. A motorhome up to 3.5 t usually pays class II.
Take care on the way to Dubrovnik: the Croatian coast is cut by Bosnia and Herzegovina at Neum, and Bosnia is not allowed. Use the Pelješac bridge, which avoids that stretch.
Worth seeing: the walled old town of Dubrovnik.

sections.h2: Greece: only by ferry from Italy
paragraphs: By land, every route to Greece goes through countries that are not allowed, either through the Balkans or through Bulgaria. The only option is the ferry from Italian Adriatic ports such as Ancona, Bari or Brindisi to Igoumenitsa or Patras, with the permission described in clause 7.4.
Greek motorways have toll booths. Worth seeing: the monasteries of Meteora.

sections.h2: Cyprus: seasonal ferry and driving on the left
paragraphs: Cyprus can only be reached by sea. In 2026 the Piraeus-Limassol ferry ran in the summer season, with a crossing of about 31 hours. Check whether there are sailings on your dates before asking for permission.
In Cyprus you drive on the left. The permission covers the Republic of Cyprus: do not cross into the north of the island with the motorhome.
Worth seeing: Aphrodite's Rock (Petra tou Romiou), near Paphos.
You get there on the Virtu Ferries ferry from Pozzallo in Sicily to Valletta; the crossing takes less than two hours.

In Malta you drive on the left and the streets are narrow. The motorhome is more comfortable at campsites and in areas outside the towns. Worth seeing: the Blue Grotto, on the south coast of the island.

sections.h2: Iceland: ferry from Denmark and tarmac only
paragraphs: The Smyril Line ferry sails from Hirtshals in Denmark to Seyðisfjörður and usually calls at the Faroe Islands. The Faroes are not on the list of authorised countries: the motorhome must not leave the ship there.
The contract forbids driving off the paved road network (clause 6.1.e). In Iceland that rules out the F mountain roads and gravel tracks. The ring road around the island is paved.
Worth seeing: the Skógafoss waterfall, right by the ring road.

sections.h2: Great Britain: ferry and driving on the left
paragraphs: From northern Spain, Brittany Ferries links Bilbao and Santander with Portsmouth and Plymouth. You can also cross from France by ferry or on the Eurotunnel train, always with written permission.

You drive on the left. In London the motorhome meets the ULEZ standard as a Euro 6 diesel, but TfL asks for foreign vehicles to be registered in advance. The Dartford Crossing, east of London, is paid online by midnight the following day.
The contract says Great Britain: if your route goes through Northern Ireland, mention it when you ask for permission. Worth seeing: Tower Bridge in London.
Brittany Ferries links Bilbao with Rosslare without going through France. Another option is the Cherbourg-Rosslare ferry.
You drive on the left. The M50 motorway around Dublin has a barrier-free toll: pay it on eflow.ie before 20:00 the following day.
Worth seeing: the Cliffs of Moher.
The motorhome may not enter these countries, not even with permission. The contract also forbids travelling to countries at war or in armed conflict (clause 7.3).

Morocco is the question we hear most often in Valencia, and the answer is no. There are two reasons. Morocco is outside the insurance territory, so the motorhome would have no own damage cover there. And getting there takes a ferry, during which the insurance does not cover that damage either. If you want to visit Morocco, cross as a foot passenger and leave the motorhome at a campsite or car park on the Spanish side.
Gibraltar is not allowed either: it is British territory that is not on the list, even though it sits right next to La Línea.
list: Albania, Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro and North Macedonia.
Bulgaria, Romania and Liechtenstein: only compulsory third-party liability insurance applies there, with no own damage cover, so they are not allowed either.

sections.h2: What happens if you go anyway
paragraphs: Entering a country that is not authorised is a material breach of the contract (clause 7.3). The owner may terminate the contract, demand the immediate return of the motorhome and, if needed, inform the authorities.

Damage and costs are yours to pay, and outside the authorised territory you lose the insurance cover. A knock that in Spain would cost you at most the 900 € excess turns into the full cost of the repair.
The same applies if you travel to one of the 29 allowed countries without written permission.

faq.q: Can I take the rental motorhome to Portugal?
faq.a: Yes, with prior written permission, which you ask for when you book or before you leave. On electronic tolls the motorhome pays as class 2: link a card to the number plate or use Via Verde Visitors, and keep the receipts. If you cannot show payment, the outstanding tolls are charged plus a 50 € handling fee.

faq.q: Can I cross to Morocco with the motorhome?
faq.a: No. Morocco is outside the insurance territory, and during the ferry crossing the insurance does not cover own damage either. Taking the motorhome there is a material breach of the contract. You can cross as a foot passenger and leave the motorhome in Spain.

faq.q: What do I need to travel to France?
faq.a: The written permission, a card for the péages (the motorhome pays class 3) and the Crit'Air sticker if you plan to enter a low emission zone such as Paris or Lyon. Order it on certificat-air.gouv.fr; a diesel from 2024 gets Crit'Air 2.

faq.q: Can I go to Andorra?
faq.a: Yes, with written permission. Andorra has no motorways and no vignette, but there are customs checks on the way in and on the way back, with limits for tobacco and alcohol.

faq.q: Can I take the motorhome to Mallorca, Ibiza or Menorca?
faq.a: Yes. The Balearic Islands are Spain, but the ferry needs prior written permission. From loading to unloading the insurance does not cover own damage or fire, and you pay any damage at its real cost.

faq.q: Which documents do I need outside Spain?
faq.a: Your driving licence, the rental contract, the written permission for the countries on your route and the vehicle documents with the insurance certificate, which stay in the motorhome. In the countries of the Multilateral Guarantee Agreement the Spanish plate counts as proof of insurance and no green card is asked for.

faq.q: Can I drive to Greece?
faq.a: Not overland: every route crosses countries that are not allowed. You go by ferry from Italy, with written permission.

faq.q: What happens if I enter a country that is not on the list?
faq.a: It is a material breach: the owner may terminate the contract and demand the motorhome back immediately, and you are liable for all damage and costs with no excess cap, because there is no own damage cover there.

cta.text: If your trip leaves Spain, tell us the countries when you book and we will prepare the written permission.
